application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client built on Fetch, with typed responses, configurable request handling, parsing, retries, hooks, and normalized errors.
application.purpose: Make HTTP requests easier to configure and consume across browser and Node.js environments.

domains.name: HTTP request execution

domains.name: Response handling and errors
domains.description: Parses response bodies, handles HTTP failures, retries eligible requests, and exposes contextual errors.

domains.name: Runtime adapters
domains.description: Provides Fetch implementations and related primitives for global and Node.js runtimes.

domains.name: Examples and tests
domains.description: Demonstrates type-safe usage and exercises client behavior.

applicationFacts: The client exports both $fetch and ofetch as names for the configured client.
The main client returns parsed data; its raw method returns the response object, and its native method calls the underlying Fetch implementation directly.
Request options support base URLs, query parameters, merged headers, timeouts, retry settings, and lifecycle hooks.
JSON-serializable bodies on payload methods are automatically stringified, with JSON Content-Type and Accept headers added when absent.
Response parsing can be selected explicitly or inferred from Content-Type; JSON is the fallback when no content type is available.
HTTP responses with status codes from 400 through 599 are treated as errors by default, unless ignoreResponseError is enabled.
By default, payload methods are not retried and other methods receive one retry; configured retry status codes default to 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504.
The package provides a Node.js adapter that can use a node-fetch-native implementation when global Fetch is unavailable.
